findings.summary: The walk through earlier links' base_jobs adds nothing, because ancestry is transitive. The criterion 5 case 2 test would pass without the walk.
findings.evidence: record_bases picks every other Open link whose head is an ancestor of job.commit. Ancestry is transitive: if A's head is an ancestor of B's and B's of C's, then A's is an ancestor of C's. So C's own record_bases already finds A, and the walk through B's base_jobs adds nothing. Step 4 says record_bases runs on an open link after loading it. In criterion 5 case 2, C's link is loaded Open, so record_bases recomputes [A, B] from real ancestry. A reconciliation that 'follows only the first recorded base' would still close A, so the failure that case 2 claims would not happen. The field is in practice the 'scan all open links' alternative that Decision 1 rejects, written down for criterion 2. Fix: Either drop the walk and state plainly that base_jobs records what the landing-time scan found, or name the shape where the walk matters and build case 2 so that record_bases cannot find A (for example, C's link already Landed when land_pr starts). Then the test fails without the walk. Make the change description match.
findings.location: Decisions 1 and 4; approach (2) 'walks base_jobs, and through each earlier link's own base_jobs the rest of the stack'; Criterion 5 case 2

findings.summary: No test isolates the first ancestry check (earlier head reachable from the merged commit). Removing it would pass every test.
findings.evidence: The second check is 'the earlier head is an ancestor of link.head'. land_pr bails unless head == job.commit (landing.rs:218), and record_bases records a base only when its head is an ancestor of job.commit. So for every recorded base whose host head has not moved, the second check already holds. In the merge-commit cases (criterion 3 case 1 uses an Edges fake that must also make e1 an ancestor of cand1 for the base to be recorded; criterion 5 case 3 uses real git), the first check is never the deciding one. Row 2 'via arm 1' is misleading. Fix: Add one case where only the first check holds: base_jobs pre-stored, and the host head an ancestor of the merged commit but not of C's head. Or drop the first check and correct the table.
findings.location: Decision 2 and commit-shape table row 2 ('CLOSED via arm 1'); Criterion 3 case 1; Criterion 5 case 3

findings.summary: One stale link with an unknown head could put a warning into every later landing.
findings.evidence: Git::is_ancestor (athena-git lib.rs:363-377) returns Err for an unknown sha. record_bases checks every Open pr-link.json under jobs/ and early-pr/, and those files persist after landing (link_path is under job_dir; adopt moves early links there). One stale Open link whose head is no longer in the local object store would put a warning into every later landing of every job. The plan does not say whether an ancestry error on another job's link is a warning or a silent 'not a base'. Fix: In record_bases, treat an ancestry error or parse error for another job's link as 'not a base' with no warning. Or warn only when that link is later judged in close_carried_prs. Add an assertion that an unrelated stale link with an unknown head adds no warning.
findings.location: Step 4 'call record_bases on an open link ... (errors become warnings)'

findings.summary: The dependents entry names the helper wrongly and omits its callers. Its 'fresh state directory' claim is wrong for them.
findings.evidence: The helper named there is land_through_pr (test_support.rs:617), not 'land_job'. It is called by CutoverFixture (test_support.rs:542) and by crates/athena-cli/tests/trailer_stop.rs:119 and :313. trailer_stop lands a second job in a state root that already holds the cutover job's link, and cutover_fixture.rs:179-186 asserts on report.warnings. Those links are Landed and filtered out, so the outcome is probably unchanged, but the stated reason is wrong and these readers are not listed. Fix: Name land_through_pr and its callers (CutoverFixture in test_support.rs, and trailer_stop.rs and cutover_fixture.rs in the athena-cli tests) in the entry. Correct the reason: other links there are Landed and skipped by the Open filter.
findings.location: Dependents: 'land_pr behavior' entry, Reason 'Those tests use a fresh state directory with no other job's link'

findings.summary: The close and comment write calls are logged in the host-error log as read-pr.
findings.evidence: HostOperation (athena-data records/core.rs:18-45) has ReadPr, logged as 'read-pr'. Logging a PATCH that closes a PR and a POST comment as read-pr mislabels write calls in the host-error log. Fix: Keep the reuse while athena-data is out of scope, but say in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG that close and comment failures are logged under read-pr. Propose a dedicated variant as a follow-up.
findings.location: Decision 5 (HostOperation::ReadPr for status, close and comment)

findings.summary: The plan does not name the history-check break that the same stacked-squash shape causes.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:2999-3003 and athena.toml:165-168: the squash of PR #130 carried two jobs' landings (20261010-154004-60r4 and another). The chain was broken, main's history check failed, and the commit needed a [history] exempt entry. This plan closes the stale PR, but a later stacked squash still carries an earlier job's landing in the same way. Fix: In the change description and CHANGELOG, name the history-check break as a related consequence that this change does not fix, and propose it as a follow-up. Do not widen the scope.
findings.location: Approach/Risks; root-cause default ('when that lies outside the job's scope, name it and propose the fix')

findings.summary: Two cargo test filters do not match the tests they are meant to run.
findings.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core base_jobs` does not match `land_pr_stores_the_bases_it_found_in_the_link`. `cargo test -p athena-core earlier_pull_request` does not match `shapes_left_open`. Fix: Rename the tests to contain the filter string, or give one Run command per test.

No code or record read in the snapshot shows which head shape PR #129 had. In the drain path, PrLander::land (drain.rs:3255) always calls land_pr, which replaces the early head with the landing commit (landing.rs:206-212). That is table row 1, not row 5. Fix: Label it an estimate, or say which flow (local `go` without `land --pr`) produces row 5.
findings.location: Risks, first bullet ('The most common stale shape stays open')

summary: I read pr.rs, landing.rs (land_pr, publish, confirm_existing_merge, Athena::land_pr), the FakeHost, Rig and leak helpers in gh/tests.rs, test_support.rs, drain.rs landing_from_report, run/mod.rs where the candidate is built, the git is_ancestor code, and the CHANGELOG entry on the PR #129/#130 squash. Every file, function and seam the plan names exists as described. The nine `PrLink {` literals match a grep. The PrHost implementors are the five the plan lists. The only reader of warnings that does anything with them is display.rs:540. GitContent fetches the merged commit, so the first ancestry check can run on real git. The approach is sound. Closing rests only on git ancestry plus the host's current PR state and head, and it fails safe: nothing is closed on an error, a moved head, or a stack that was replayed under new hashes. The squash-merge check is justified and goes to the user as an open question. Each criterion has a demonstration on the production `land_pr`, and each would fail if the behavior were removed. The commit-shape table and the real-git branch fixture are present. Athena's six out-of-deliverable findings are compile-forced one-line edits plus the one doc that lists the link's fields. I agree they are minor. I found nothing blocking. The minor problems: (1) the recorded `base_jobs` and the walk through earlier links add nothing beyond a scan, because ancestry is transitive, and the walk test would not fail without the walk; (2) no test isolates the first ancestry check; (3) how errors from reading other jobs' links are reported can make landings noisy; (4) the dependents claim "fresh state directory" is wrong for land_through_pr callers; (5) writes are logged as read-pr; (6) some test-name filters do not match the tests they name; (7) the history-check break that the same squash shape causes is not named.
